children: What if, instead of deciding to invest Rs 5,000 a month in gold, you could start with a target of how many grams you eventually want to accumulate?

Axis Mutual Fund has launched ‘Shagun SIP’, a digital feature that allows investors to set systematic investment targets for gold and silver in terms of grams. The facility, launched on August 31, is available for investments in Axis Gold Fund and Axis Silver Fund of Fund.

The feature essentially adds a goal-based layer to a regular systematic investment plan (SIP). Investors can decide the quantity of gold or silver they want to accumulate and the period over which they want to do so. The system then calculates the investment required based on the metal price.

Say an investor wants to build an investment equivalent to a certain quantity of gold over several years. Instead of fixing the SIP at a particular rupee amount throughout the period, Shagun SIP links the investment to the targeted quantity in grams.
Since gold and silver prices change over time, the rupee amount required to buy the targeted quantity can also change.
According to Axis Mutual Fund, investors can set accumulation targets of up to 25 kg for gold and 50 kg for silver.
However, there is an important distinction: investors are not directly buying physical gold or silver through the feature.

Shagun SIP routes investments into Axis Gold Fund or Axis Silver Fund of Fund. Axis Gold Fund invests predominantly in units of Axis Gold ETF, while Axis Silver Fund of Fund similarly invests predominantly in Axis Silver ETF. This means investors ultimately hold mutual fund units rather than physical metal.
How is this different from a regular gold or silver SIP?
Investors could already run conventional SIPs in both schemes. Axis Gold Fund, for instance, allows SIP investments and has a minimum investment amount of Rs 100.
The difference with Shagun SIP is primarily in how the goal is set.

With a conventional SIP, an investor may decide to invest, say, Rs 2,000 every month. Under the new feature, the starting point can instead be the quantity of gold or silver the investor wants to accumulate over a chosen period.
This can make the feature relevant for investors who think of precious-metal goals in terms of grams, particularly for long-term goals where a certain quantity of gold is being targeted.

“Shagun SIP offers a fully digital, goal-based experience for investors looking to build gold and silver holdings systematically over the long term,” said Boniface Noronha, Chief Digital Officer at Axis Mutual Fund.
As with any gold or silver fund, however, the eventual value of the investment will remain linked to movements in the underlying metal prices and the performance of the respective schemes.
